scheme_name: Subsidy Scheme on Establishment of 25 R.I.R. Bird’s unit 40 R.I.R. Bird’s Unit and Stipend for Poultry Farming Training
description:
The Subsidy Scheme on Establishment of 25 R.I.R. Bird’s Unit and 40 R.I.R. Bird’s Unit along with Stipend for Poultry Farming Training is a significant initiative by the Government of India aimed at promoting poultry farming among rural and semi-urban populations.

This scheme was launched in the year 2021 as part of the government's broader strategy to enhance the livelihoods of farmers and promote self-employment opportunities in the agricultural sector.

The primary objective of this scheme is to encourage individuals to establish their own poultry units by providing financial assistance and training.

The scheme specifically targets the establishment of poultry units consisting of either 25 or 40 Rhode Island Red (R.I.R.) birds.

The Rhode Island Red breed is known for its high egg production capacity and adaptability to various climatic conditions.

Under this scheme, the government provides a subsidy of 50 percent of the total project cost for setting up a poultry unit.

The maximum subsidy amount is capped at INR 50,000 for the establishment of a 25-bird unit.

For the 40-bird unit, the maximum subsidy amount is set at INR 75,000.

The scheme also includes a stipend for individuals undergoing poultry farming training.

The stipend amount is INR 500 per day for a duration of 15 days.

This training is designed to equip beneficiaries with essential skills and knowledge related to poultry farming.

The training covers various aspects including feeding, health management, and biosecurity measures.

Eligibility criteria for the scheme are clearly defined to ensure that the benefits reach the intended beneficiaries.

Applicants must be residents of India and should preferably belong to rural or semi-urban areas.

The age limit for applicants is set between 18 years and 55 years.

There are no specific educational qualifications required for applying to this scheme.

However, applicants must demonstrate a genuine interest in poultry farming.

Income criteria are also established to prioritize economically weaker sections of society.

Applicants from families with an annual income of less than INR 3 lakhs are given preference.

The application process for this scheme involves several steps to ensure transparency and accountability.

Interested individuals must first approach the nearest Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying office.

They need to fill out an application form which can be obtained from the office or downloaded from the official website.

Along with the application form, applicants must submit a copy of their Aadhaar card for identity verification.

Proof of residence such as a utility bill or a rental agreement is also required.

Additionally, applicants must provide a detailed project report outlining the proposed poultry unit.

This report should include the estimated costs, expected income, and the management plan for the poultry unit.

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by a committee formed by the Department of Animal Husbandry.

The committee will assess the feasibility of the project and the eligibility of the applicant.

If approved, the subsidy amount will be disbursed directly to the applicant's bank account.

The training program is conducted in collaboration with various agricultural universities and institutes.

The training sessions are typically held at designated centers across the country.

The frequency of training sessions may vary depending on the demand and availability of resources.

Disbursement of the subsidy is generally done within 30 days of approval of the application.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying under the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

The contact details for the Department can be found on their official website.

This scheme is part of the larger initiative to boost the poultry sector in India which has been growing steadily over the years.

According to the 20th Livestock Census conducted in 2019, India has approximately 851.81 million poultry birds.

The poultry sector contributes significantly to the agricultural GDP of the country.

The government aims to increase poultry production by providing necessary support and incentives to farmers.

The scheme is expected to create job opportunities and enhance food security in rural areas.

By promoting poultry farming, the government also aims to improve the nutritional standards of the population.

The scheme aligns with the National Livestock Mission which was launched in 2014 to promote sustainable growth in the livestock sector.

The poultry farming training program is designed to ensure that beneficiaries are well-equipped to manage their units effectively.

The training includes practical sessions where participants can gain hands-on experience in poultry management.

The government also encourages the use of modern techniques and practices in poultry farming.

This includes the use of quality feed and vaccination to ensure the health of the birds.

The scheme is expected to benefit thousands of individuals across the country.

It is particularly beneficial for women and marginalized communities who are looking for self-employment opportunities.

The establishment of poultry units can lead to increased income and improved livelihoods for families.

The government is committed to monitoring the progress of the scheme and making necessary adjustments based on feedback from beneficiaries.

In conclusion, the Subsidy Scheme on Establishment of 25 R.I.R. Bird’s Unit and 40 R.I.R. Bird’s Unit along with Stipend for Poultry Farming Training is a comprehensive initiative aimed at promoting poultry farming in India.

By providing financial assistance and training, the government aims to empower individuals and enhance their economic prospects.

This scheme not only supports the establishment of poultry units but also fosters a culture of entrepreneurship among rural populations.

The emphasis on training ensures that beneficiaries are well-prepared to succeed in their poultry farming endeavors.

Overall, this scheme represents a significant step towards achieving self-sufficiency in poultry production and improving the livelihoods of farmers in India.
